title: One parsed source, for psyche relate --parse
description: A source that another program fetched and parsed, which `psyche relate --parse` connects to personal context without fetching it again. psyche refuses a document carrying any key this schema does not declare, naming the key. Each new key in this schema raises schema_version. A psyche release reads the new version and the one before it, and a writer sends the new version only once that release is installed.

key.description: The source's stable id in the program that parsed it. A URL serves where there is no other.

url.description: Where the source lives, and null where it has no address, such as text typed by hand.

zone.description: Who wrote the text. outside is anyone else, even where you shared the link, and owner is you.

media_type.description: The source's media type before it was parsed, such as text/html.

extractor.description: The program that turned the source into text, such as pandoc.

text.description: The source as plain text, which is what relate reads. Whitespace alone is refused, because it leaves nothing to relate.

units.description: The text's structure: each page, chapter, section or post, numbered from 1 in reading order. A finding's unit names one.

rules_version.description: The version of the rules a scanner read the text with, and null where nothing scanned it.

findings.description: What a scanner flagged in the text, such as an instruction aimed at a model or Unicode that hides text from a person. An empty list says nothing was flagged.

rule.description: The id of the rule that matched.

span.description: The text the rule matched, which a scanner may cut short.

unit.description: The unit the match starts in, and null where the text has no units.

offset.description: Where the match starts, in bytes from its unit's start, or from the text's.

suggested.description: Each command, link and piece of code the text suggests a reader run, open or paste, listed apart from the findings.

enriched.description: What another reader derived from the text before psyche saw it. Every key is optional.

idea.description: One sentence stating the source's idea.

suggestion.description: One change the source suggests, in a sentence.

genre.description: What kind of writing it is, such as tutorial or opinion.

themes.description: What the source argues or explores.

quality.description: A rough estimate of its quality, from 1 to 10.
